The example in question b (Sam, a baker in Orange, NSW) should be replaced with a Victorian local example, such as a business in a Victorian town or suburb.
match.reason: The bank card covers the same idea of why people start businesses (independence, profit, meeting needs) at a suitable Year 11 depth, but it adds risk and skills-and-money weighing and uses NSW examples, so it needs light adaptation for the VCE course.

confirm.reason: The closest bank point, 'The decision to start a business', is broader: half its card and one question are about weighing skills, money and risk. draft.title: Why people start a business
card: People start a business for different reasons. Three common ones are independence, profit and meeting a need.
Independence
the wish to be your own boss. The owner decides what to sell, how to work and when to work.
Profit
the wish to earn more than the business costs to run. Profit is income minus expenses, and it can give the owner a better income than a wage.
Meeting a need
the wish to supply something that people in the market or community lack. An example is a bakery that opens in a town with no bakery.
draft.remember: Owners start a business to be independent, to make a profit, or to meet a need.

a.q: Priya leaves her job to open a gym in her town because the nearest gym is 60 km away. Which reason for starting a business is clearest?
opts: To meet a need in the community
To make a profit above all else
To gain independence from a boss
To earn more than she did as an employee
a.why: Priya saw that her town lacked a gym and opened one to fill that gap, so she is meeting a need. Profit or independence may also matter to her, but nothing in the case points to them.
a.clue: What was missing in her town?

b.q: Tom is a chef who is tired of his head chef changing his menus. He opens his own café so he can decide the menu himself. Which reason fits best?
opts: Independence, because he wants to make his own decisions
Profit, because he wants to earn more than his wage
Meeting a need, because the area has too few cafés
Profit, because chefs earn more as business owners
b.why: Tom's main aim is to control his own menu and decisions, which is independence. Profit is tempting because any café hopes to earn money, but the case gives no sign that earning more drives his choice.
b.clue: Look at what he is trying to get away from.

a.best: To meet a need in the community

b.best: Independence, because he wants to make his own decisions

problems.detail: The card says these are three common reasons among many ('different reasons... three common ones'). The remember line drops 'common' and lists them as if they were the only reasons owners start a business.
